Subject: Packaging question — balancing seats vs throughput for bursty imaging workflows

Hi Marcus,

Quick context: our ML team at Sapphire is ramping a new imaging pipeline that has long quiet periods but frequent short bursts (weekly ingest windows, then spikes). Current usage is modest but projected to jump 3–4x in two quarters. We want a pricing/packaging approach that avoids overpaying during quiet weeks but preserves low latency for spikes.

Specifically:
- Is there a hybrid option (base reserved throughput + burst credits) that lets us keep per-token costs predictable?
- How do feature bundles (KV cache, prioritized routing) map to tiers — can we pick throughput from one tier and feature set from another?
- If we need to step down after a pilot, what does the rollback look like for prorates/credits?

Attaching a short snapshot of our Q3 usage. Would love a short proposal and a recommended path to pilot.

Thanks —
Elena
Elena Mora
Director, ML Platform
Sapphire Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Mora <elena.mora@sapphirehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — balancing seats vs throughput for bursty imaging workflows

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the usage snapshot — very helpful. Short answers up front: yes, we have a hybrid approach that fits this profile and a couple of safe rollback paths. I pulled together a two-page starter proposal (attached) and a quick playbook below. If that looks good, we can schedule a 30-min scoping call and include procurement.

Playbook summary:
1) Pilot configuration: small reserved baseline (light GPU pool) + burst credits bucket (monthly top-up), with prefix/KV caching enabled to keep latency low for repeated prompts.
2) Feature mapping: routing and prioritization are configurable per route — you can enable prioritized routing for the imaging inference route while leaving other routes on standard throughput. That means feature bundles are independent of the baseline throughput tier (we map features at the route level).
3) Downgrade/rollback: Step-downs happen at the billing period boundary. We offer two rollback options: a) temporary freeze of burst top-ups for the next cycle (no refund) or b) prorated credit toward future months if you commit to a 3-month rebaseline. Both options are documented in the attached matrix.

Estimated economics (very high level):
- Baseline reserved pool sized to 25% of your peak: predictable monthly commit, lowest per-token cost for baseline traffic.
- Burst credits: pay-as-you-go or pre-purchased packs (cheaper if pre-bought); automatically consumed when baseline is saturated.

Attaching: RI-proposed-tier-matrix-v1.pdf (proposal + rollback matrix). Can you confirm availability Tuesday/Wednesday for a 30-min call to validate assumptions and scoping?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
Attachment: RI-proposed-tier-matrix-v1.pdf

Kimberly / Ben —

Forwarding Elena's note and my quick plan. Two asks:
1) Kimberly: can you confirm the pricing math on baseline=25% peak + 2x monthly burst pack vs pure reserved at 50%? I sketched numbers on page 2 of the attached; would like your sanity check before I send to procurement.
2) Ben: procurement side — if they prefer pre-purchased burst credits, what concession should we offer on packs for a first-year committed customer (Sapphire has an enterprise pilot track)? I want to propose a one-time onboarding credit + a 10% off burst-pack rate for the first 6 months. Are we comfortable?

Note: we should keep the feature routing decoupled so there's no migration dependency if they change throughput later.

Cheers,
Marcus

Marcus — quick checks below. Numbers are illustrative; I can send a spreadsheet if you want exact line items.

Baseline(25% of projected peak) + 2x burst-pack: ~28% lower expected annual cost vs choosing a 50% reserved slab if their spikes are intermittent (which they are per the CSV). The win comes from burst-only consumption at peak minutes rather than paying reserved for idle capacity.

If they pre-purchase burst packs, 10% off for the first 6 months + a one-time onboarding credit ($5k) sounds reasonable for an enterprise pilot. That gives them predictable unit economics and reduces churn risk.

Two operational notes:
- Make sure we enable per-route KV caching for the imaging pipeline — will save tokens on repeated segments and favors the baseline model.
- Add an automatic telemetry alert if burst consumption exceeds 60% of the pack in any given week so we can proactively propose a slab increase.

I can prep the detailed pricing table and send it to you by EOD.

—Kimberly

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the data. Attached is a short, concrete pilot proposal and price sketch based on our baseline + burst-pack approach. Highlights:
- Baseline reserved: capacity sized ~25% of projected peak (gives low per-token baseline).
- Burst packs: pre-purchase option with 10% discount for the first 6 months + a $5,000 onboarding credit if you sign pilot paperwork within 30 days.
- Features: route-level prioritized routing and KV caching enabled for imaging; no need to align feature bundles to the baseline tier.
- Rollback: step-down at billing boundary with option for prorated credit if you elect 3-month rebaseline commitment.

Next steps:

2) Schedule a 30-min call to confirm exact baseline sizing and final pricing.
